source_text:
Ἐνετειλάμην σοι, φησίν, ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐντολῇ, ἵνα φυλάξῃς τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. Ναί, φημί, κύριε. Ἀλλὰ νῦν θέλω σοι, φησίν, δηλῶσαι καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτῶν, ἵνα νοήσῃς τίς αὐτῶν τίνα δύναμιν ἔχει καὶ ἐνέργειαν: διπλαῖ γάρ εἰσιν αἱ ἐνέργειαι αὐτῶν. κεῖνται οὖν ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ:
σὺ οὖν πίστευε τῷ δικαίῳ, τῷ δὲ ἀδίκῳ μὴ πιστεύσῃς: τὸ γὰρ δίκαιον ὀρθὴν ὁδὸν ἔχει, τὸ δὲ ἄδικον στρεβλήν. ἀλλὰ σὺ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορεύου καὶ ὁμαλῇ, τὴν δὲ στρεβλὴν ἔασον.
ἡ γὰρ στρεβλὴ ὁδὸς τρίβους οὐκ ἔχει, ἀλλ’ ἀνοδίας καὶ προσκόμματα πολλὰ καὶ τραχεῖά ἐστι καὶ ἀκανθώδης. βλαβερὰ οὖν ἐστι τοῖς ἐν αὐτῇ πορευομένοις.
οἱ δὲ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορευόμενοι ὁμαλῶς περιπατοῦσι καὶ ἀπροσκόπως: οὔτε γὰρ τραχεῖά ἐστιν οὔτε ἀκανθώδης. βλέπεις οὖν, ὅτι συμφορώτερόν ἐστι ταύτῃ τῇ ὁδῷ πορεύεσθαι.
Ἀρέσκει μοι, φημί, κύριε, ταύτῃ τῇ ὁδῷ πορεύεσθαι. Πορεύσῃ, φησί, καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς κύριον, πορεύσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.
Ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τῆς πίστεως. δύο εἰσὶν ἄγγελοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, εἷς τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ εἷς τῆς πονηρίας.
Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, γνώσομαι τὰς αὐτῶν ἐνεργείας, ὅτι ἀμφότεροι ἄγγελοι μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατοικοῦσιν;
Ἄκουε, φησί, καὶ συνιεῖς αὐτάς. ὁ μὲν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἄγγελος τρυφερός ἐστι καὶ αἰσχυντηρὸς καὶ πραῢς καὶ ἡσύχιος: ὅταν οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, εὐθέως λαλεῖ μετὰ σοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης, περὶ ἁγνείας, περὶ σεμνότητος καὶ περὶ αὐταρκείας καὶ περὶ παντός ἔργου δικαίου καὶ περὶ πάσης ἀρετῆς ἐνδόξου. ταῦτα πάντα ὅταν εἰς τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ , γίνωσκε, ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς δικαιοσύνης μετὰ σοῦ ἐστί. ταῦτα οὖν ἐστι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης. τούτῳ οὖν πίστευε καὶ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ.
ὅρα οὖν καὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας τὰ ἔργα. πρῶτον πάντων ὀξύχολός ἐστι καὶ πικρὸς καὶ ἄφρων, καὶ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά, καταστρέφοντα τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ: ὅταν οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γνῶθι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ.
Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, νοήσω αὐτόν, οὐκ ἐπίσταμαι. Ἄκουε, φησίν. ὅταν ὀξυχολία σοί τις προσπέσῃ ἢ πικρία, γίνωσκε, ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν σοί: εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλειαι ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν καὶ ποικίλων τροφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων καὶ ἐπιθυμίαι γυναικῶν καὶ πλεονεξιῶν καὶ ὑπερηφανία πολλή τις καὶ ἀλαζονεία καὶ ὅσα τούτοις παραπλήσιά ἐστι καὶ ὅμοια: ταῦτα οὖν ὅταν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε, ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς πονηρίας ἐστὶν ἐν σοί.
σὺ οὖν ἐπιγνοὺς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἀπόστα ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, μηδὲν αὐτῷ πίστευε, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά εἰσι καὶ ἀσύμποφα τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ. ἔχεις οὖν ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰς ἐνεργείας: σύνιε αὐτὰς καὶ πίστευε τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης:
ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας ἀπόστηθι, ὅτι ἡ διδαχὴ αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι παντὶ ἔργῳ: ἐὰν γὰρ ᾖ τις πιστὸς ἀνὴρ καὶ ἡ ἐνθύμησις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τούτου ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, δεῖ τὸν ἄνδρα ἐκεῖνον ἢ τὴν γυναῖκα ἐξαμαρτῆσαί τι.
ἐὰν δὲ πάλιν πονηρότατός τις ᾖ ἀνὴρ ἢ γυνὴ καὶ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἐξ ἀνάγκης δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀγαθόν τι ποιῆσαι.
βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι καλόν ἐστι τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἀκολουθεῖν, τῷ δὲ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς πονηρίας ἀποτάξασθαι.
τὰ μὲν περὶ τῆς πίστεως αὕτη ἡ ἐντολὴ δηλοῖ, ἵνα τοῖς ἔργοις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης πιστεύσῃς, καὶ ἐργασάμενος αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ. πίστευε δέ, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας χαλεπά ἐστι: μὴ ἐργαζόμενος οὖν αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ.
thought_title: The two angels and their works
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the sixth commandment. Two angels stay with every person, one of righteousness and one of wickedness, and Hermas learns to tell them apart by what each stirs up in the heart.
pass_a_gloss: I commanded you, he says, in the first commandment, that you keep faith and fear and self-control. Yes, I say, lord. But now I want, he says, to show you also their powers, so that you may understand which of them has what power and working: for their workings are double. They lie then upon the righteous and the unrighteous: you then believe the righteous, but do not believe the unrighteous: for the righteous has a straight way, but the unrighteous a crooked one. But you walk in the straight way and smooth, and leave the crooked one. For the crooked way has no paths, but is pathless and has many stumbling blocks and is rough and thorny. It is harmful then to those walking in it. But those walking in the straight way walk smoothly and without stumbling: for it is neither rough nor thorny. You see then, that it is more advantageous to walk in this way. It pleases me, I say, lord, to walk in this way. You will walk, he says, and whoever turns to the Lord from a whole heart will walk in it. Hear now, he says, about faith. There are two angels with the human being, one of righteousness and one of wickedness. How then, I say, lord, will I know their workings, since both angels dwell with me? Hear, he says, and you will understand them. The angel of righteousness is gentle and modest and meek and quiet: whenever then this one comes up upon your heart, immediately he speaks with you about righteousness, about purity, about dignity and about contentment and about every righteous work and about every glorious virtue. Whenever all these things come up into your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. These then are the works of the angel of righteousness. Believe then this one and his works. See then also the works of the angel of wickedness. First of all he is quick-tempered and bitter and foolish, and his works are evil, destroying the servants of God: whenever then this one comes up upon your heart, know him from his works. How, I say, lord, will I understand him, I do not know. Hear, he says. Whenever some anger falls upon you or bitterness, know that he is in you: then desire of many deeds and extravagances of many foods and of drunkennesses and of many carousings and of varied foods and of things not fitting and desires of women and of greedy gains and much great arrogance and boastfulness and as many things as are close to these and similar: whenever then these things come up upon your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you. You then, having recognized his works, stand away from him, do not believe him at all, because his works are evil and unprofitable to the servants of God. You have then the workings of both angels: understand them and believe the angel of righteousness: but from the angel of wickedness stand away, because his teaching is evil in every work: for if any man is faithful and the thought of this angel comes up upon his heart, that man or that woman must commit some sin. But if again any man or woman is most wicked and the works of the angel of righteousness come up upon his heart, of necessity he must do something good. You see then, he says, that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness, but to renounce the angel of wickedness. The things about faith this commandment makes clear, so that you may believe the works of the angel of righteousness, and having worked them you may live to God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are harsh: not working them then you will live to God.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term; the Shepherd refers back to the first commandment's triad of faith, fear, and self-control.
The Shepherd distinguishes the active operations of the two angels; 'workings' preserves the dynamic force of the Greek noun.
The way imagery contrasts straight and crooked paths; 'crooked' keeps the physical metaphor vivid.
The Greek noun means absence of paths; 'pathless' renders the privative force directly.
The adverb describes smooth walking on the straight way; the rendering keeps the negation of stumbling explicit.
The verb means to take leave of or renounce; 'renounce' fits the moral contrast with following the angel of righteousness.

pass_b_english: “In the first commandment,” the Shepherd said, “I commanded you to guard faith and fear and self-control.” “Yes, sir,” I said. “But now,” he said, “I want to show you their powers as well, so that you may understand what power each of them has, and how it works. For their workings are twofold. They bear on what is righteous and on what is unrighteous.

“So put your faith in what is righteous, and put no faith in what is unrighteous. For what is righteous has a straight way, but what is unrighteous has a crooked one. As for you, walk in the straight and level way, and leave the crooked way alone. For the crooked way has no beaten paths. It is trackless ground, full of stumbling blocks, and it is rough and thorny. So it does harm to those who walk in it. But those who walk in the straight way walk smoothly and without stumbling, for it is neither rough nor thorny. You see, then, that it is better to walk in this way.”

“Sir,” I said, “I am glad to walk in this way.” “You will walk in it,” he said, “and whoever turns to the Lord with a whole heart will walk in it. Now hear,” he said, “about faith. There are two angels with a person, one of righteousness and one of wickedness.”
“How then, sir,” I said, “am I to know their workings, since both angels dwell with me?”

“Listen,” he said, “and you will understand them. The angel of righteousness is tender and modest, gentle and quiet. So when this angel rises in your heart, at once he speaks with you about righteousness, about purity, about reverence, about contentment, about every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things rise in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. These, then, are the works of the angel of righteousness. So put your faith in him and in his works.

“Now look at the works of the angel of wickedness as well. First of all, he is angry and bitter and senseless, and his works are evil. They overthrow the servants of God. So when this angel rises in your heart, know him by his works.”

“Sir,” I said, “I do not know how I am to recognize him.” “Listen,” he said. “When some anger comes over you, or bitterness, know that he is in you. Then comes the desire for many activities, and extravagance in many kinds of food and strong drink, in much carousing, and in foods that are varied and not needed. Then come desires for women, and greed, and great pride, and boastfulness, and everything close to these and like them. So when these things rise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you.

“So when you recognize his works, draw away from him and put no faith in him at all, because his works are evil and unprofitable for the servants of God. Now you have the workings of both angels. Understand them, and put your faith in the angel of righteousness. But draw away from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is evil in every deed. For if a man is faithful, and the thought of this angel rises in his heart, that man, or that woman, must commit some sin. And again, if a man or a woman is very wicked, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise in that person’s heart, then of necessity that person must do something good.

“You see, then,” he said, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and to renounce the angel of wickedness. This commandment makes plain what concerns faith, so that you may put your faith in the works of the angel of righteousness, and by doing them you will live to God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are dangerous. So by not doing them you will live to God.”

problems.why: Self-sufficiency in 11 seems to mean contentment/autarky, not the same virtue as self-control/enkrateia elsewhere.
problems.fix: Use 'contentment' or 'self-sufficiency' consistently for Greek autarkeia.

problems.why: Elect, saints, and 'called' seem to overlap but may not be identical categories; reader cannot tell if these are synonyms or distinct groups.
problems.fix: Note whether 'elect' and 'saints' are being used interchangeably or distinctly.

problems.why: In list of angel of righteousness's works, 'self-sufficiency' seems out of place as a virtue; likely means 'contentment' or 'independence from worldly needs,' not arrogance.
problems.fix: Use 'contentment' or 'inner sufficiency' to avoid modern negative connotation.

fixed: Changed 'self-sufficiency' to 'contentment' in the list of the angel of righteousness's works, since the Greek 'αὐταρκείας' here means contentment/autarky, not the same virtue as self-control (ἐγκράτεια).
The 'elect' problem is not a mistranslation in this section; the source does not use 'ἐκλεκτοί' here, so no edit is needed.
The 'self-sufficiency' problem is the same as the first; fixed with 'contentment'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'simplicity' for ἁπλότης; αὐταρκείας here means self-sufficiency/contentment, not simplicity.
last_rejected.ruling: αὐταρκείας means self-sufficiency/contentment; 'self-sufficiency' is correct. No glossary break shown.

last_rejected.why: Glossary bans 'quick temper' and requires 'anger' for ὀξυχολία; 'quick-tempered' violates glossary.
last_rejected.fix: he is anger and bitter and foolish
last_rejected.ruling: ὀξύχολός means quick-tempered; rendering is within normal range. No evidence of glossary violation.

last_rejected.why: ἀσύμποφα means 'unprofitable/harmful' but 'unprofitable' loses the sense of 'incompatible/unfitting' with God's servants.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀσύμποφα can mean unprofitable/harmful; rendering is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: χαλεπά means 'difficult, hard, grievous' not 'harsh'; 'harsh' mischaracterizes the works as severe rather than burdensome/dangerous.
last_rejected.ruling: χαλεπά can mean harsh/grievous; 'harsh' is within normal range, not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.why: ἀπόστα is imperative 'stand away/depart'; 'stand away' is awkward and unclear; 'keep away' or 'withdraw' better.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπόστα means stand away/depart; 'stand away' is acceptable English within normal range.

last_rejected.why: Same issue: ἀπόστηθι is 'withdraw/depart'; 'stand away from' is awkward and unclear.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπόστηθι means stand away/depart; 'stand away from' is acceptable within normal range.
